items.title: Attempted murder charges laid against Mississauga man, 2 others in Ontario shooting
items.summary: A Mississauga man is among three people charged with attempted murder in connection with a home invasion and shooting late last year west of the Greater Toronto Area. Ontario Provincial Police said those arrested face numerous charges after one person was shot in the early morning hours of Nov. 16, 2025 at a home south of Guelph in Puslinch Township. m. Upon arrival, they found one person suffering from a gunshot wound. The victim was rushed to a local trauma centre and later recovered from their injuries. Police arrested two people in June and charged them in connection with their investigation into the home invasion and shooting. A third person was arrested on Sept. 9. Lavontae Bowleg, 20, of Mississauga, is charged with attempt to commit murder using a restricted firearm or prohibited firearm, conspiracy to commit an indictable offence, discharge firearm with intent, breaking and entering to commit an indictable offence, possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000 and several other firearm-related offences. Police said the accused remains in custody and is scheduled to appear in Guelph court on Oct. 9. An 18-year-old from Oshawa, who was a youth at the time of the incident and therefore cannot be named, is charged with attempt to commit murder using a restricted firearm or prohibited firearm, conspiracy to commit an indictable offence, breaking and entering to commit an indictable offence and possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000.

items.title: House of the week: 3-bedroom home for under $900K in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A semi-detached home in a sought-after, family-friendly Mississauga neighbourhood. Upstairs, the primary bedroom comes with a ceiling fan, walk-in closet and a four-piece ensuite bathroom featuring a walk-in shower, soaker tub, and striking green tiled finishes. This home is close to Meadowvale Town Centre, Lake Aquitaine Park, Lisgar GO, Meadowvale Community Centre, schools, trails and major highways 401 and 407.

items.title: Staying active outdoors doesn’t have to end with colder weather
items.summary: October is Pedestrian Safety Month and International Walk to School Month. All road users are reminded to stay vigilant especially with shorter daylight hours. Taking advantage of fall weather can be a great opportunity to continue to stay active outdoors. This Pedestrian Safety Month and International Walk to School Month, the City is raising awareness about pedestrian safety and reminding all road users of their responsibilities on the road. The City is also encouraging students to use active transportation safely on their way to and from school. For students and families that want to stay active during this season, walking, cycling or rolling to and from school is a great way to build physical activity into your routine. The City has a School Walking Routes program that promotes active travel, such as walking or travelling by bike, wheelchair or other mobility devices, to and from school. School Route signs installed around the neighbourhood guide students on their way to school and alert drivers to watch for children. Remember to dress for the weather. The risk of collisions increases when daylight hours shorten. Visibility is reduced when it’s dark, making it harder to see people on the road. Some road users face a higher risk of being seriously hurt in a crash. This includes pedestrians, cyclists and e-scooter riders. items.title: Builders Who Funded Parrish's Campaign Later Won Seats on Her Housing Task Force
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish created a Housing Task Force shortly after winning the 2024 mayoral by-election that followed Bonnie Crombie's departure to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. Parrish had campaigned on making housing more affordable, and the task force was meant to cut the red tape developers face so homes could get built faster. The Pointer's review of Parrish's campaign finance disclosures found that several developers who later sat on that task force had also donated to her election campaign, within the province's $1,200 per-person contribution limit. The family behind TACC Developments, the DeGasperis family, appears three times on her donor list under that company name, the outlet reports. Kaneff Development, a longtime force in Mississauga's residential construction scene, donated through nine separate individuals totalling $10,800 before later being added to Parrish's roster of task force developers. The Pointer frames the overlap as part of a broader question about who will ultimately cover the city's multi-billion-dollar infrastructure funding gap as development fees continue to be reduced.

items.title: City Crews Pull 250 Illegal Election Signs on First Day of Bylaw Enforcement Alone
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city crews are removing more illegally placed election signs this municipal campaign than in past years, officials say. City spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told the outlet that workers removed roughly 250 illegally placed signs on Monday alone, the first day of election sign bylaw enforcement, and crews have kept up that work in the days since. McCutcheon said various campaign teams, working on behalf of mayoral, council and school board candidates, have placed signs in locations that violate the city's sign bylaw, though she cautioned the comparison to past elections hasn't been confirmed through a formal data review. City officials declined to single out any particular candidate or campaign, saying staff have collected non-compliant signs tied to a variety of campaigns. Mayor Carolyn Parrish asked senior city staff this week about enforcing the sign bylaw as it applies to candidates' own signage. She noted that a number of signs belonging to the campaign of her predecessor and main rival, Bonnie Crombie, were illegally placed as of early Sunday morning, the first day signs were allowed to go up.
